output.evaluation_rationale:

The combination of a 100% cost score (indicating the lowest price relative to the benchmark) and a 100% delivery score (perfect on‑time performance) drives the bulk of its weighted total, and the strong ancillary scores push the overall result to 97.5. 

The trade‑off analysis shows that while PRO‑SUP‑02 and PRO‑SUP‑03 offer lower cost scores (82.58 and 69.6 respectively), they do not gain enough advantage in other dimensions to offset the cost penalty. Both maintain a perfect delivery score, but their risk scores drop to 90 and 75, reflecting higher perceived supply‑chain or operational risk. Because the weighting scheme rewards cost heavily, any reduction in cost must be balanced by equal or greater improvements in risk, contract or capability to keep the total score competitive. In this case, the modest cost savings of PRO‑SUP‑02 (≈17.4 points lower than the top supplier) translate into a total weighted score that is 7.1 points lower, illustrating that aggressive cost cuts can be outweighed by increased risk or marginal differences in other pillars. The spread (14.64 points) indicates a clear performance gap, confirming that the top supplier delivers the best overall value when cost, delivery reliability, and risk are jointly considered.
